articles.title: Icons, new stars and First Nations excellence: 10 key shows from New Zealand fashion week
articles.summary: The event feted its 25 year anniversary with labels like Zambesi, promising emerging designers and an explosion of Māori and Indigenous culture. New Zealand fashion week took place in Auckland this week at the heritage-listed Shed 10 on Waitemata harbour and other venues across the city.
body: The queen of Kiwi cool, Karen Walker, staged a takeover of the Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tamaki on Wednesday evening to present a showcase called the Grand Tour which featured “current, future and archival” looks from the Karen Walker label, alongside sneakers and streetwear designed for her longtime collaborators Adidas Originals and Levi’s, including customised Japanese denim pieces for Levi’s Blue Tab line.

Aotearoa’s most exciting “new” fashion name, Claudia Li is a Chinese-New Zealander who studied at London’s Central Saint Martins and later worked with JW Anderson and Brandon Maxwell on the Haus of Gaga label, before launching her eponymous line in New York in 2015. Her label has been worn by notables including Michelle Obama, Bella Hadid and Lady Gaga. Li now calls Auckland home once again, after returning during the Covid-19 pandemic. Known for her romantic, full-blown silhouettes, she unveiled a brand new made to order collection of sculptural silk taffeta wedding dresses and occasion wear.

articles.title: A party, 101 princesses and an eccentric millionaire: Jon Ronson on a mysterious castle – and what it taught him about masculinity in crisis
articles.summary: When my son texted me from a Connecticut fortress in the middle of the night with an alarming message, it set me on a quest to understand the bizarre lifestyle of its owner.
body: I awoke one morning in the summer of 2023 to discover that, while I’d slept, my son Joel had been texting my wife and me a series of unnerving messages about a perilous situation he had found himself in, in Connecticut.

From what I could tell, as I frantically tried to piece together the night’s events, one of Joel’s friends had been invited to a party being held by a stranger she’d met that week on Tinder. So Joel and two others went along for the ride. But when they arrived, they found the man’s home so bizarre that Joel did something he’d never done before – he sent me the coordinates of his location and a photograph, just in case.

The photograph was of a vast medieval castle with a drawbridge, gargoyles and many – I couldn’t shake the sense that there were too many – spires, towers and turrets, reaching like skeletal fingers to the looming clouds above.

“I honestly have no clue what is going on,” read Joel’s second text. “This is very weird.” Then: “You drive down a road in the middle of a forest and then there’s this gate and it’s just a huge, massive castle.”

articles.title: Ditch the giant handbag, don’t overdo the botox and 16 other ways to extend your ‘hotspan’
articles.summary: If ‘lifespan’ is the time you’re alive and ‘healthspan’ the years you’re disease-free, then ‘hotspan’ is the period you’re attractive and vibrant. Want to increase yours? Experts share their tips.
body: Forget 12-step skincare routines, red light therapy and injectables – the single most important thing you can do for your skin is wear UV protection. “Not just sun protection, but UV protection, every single day, regardless of weather or season,” says Dr Jennifer Owens, resident aesthetic expert at the Reborne Longevity clinic in London. “Up to 90% of visible skin ageing is caused by UV exposure – nothing else comes close in terms of impact.”

Beware the misguided logo, warns Guardian fashion columnist Jess Cartner-Morley: “Never, ever wear a sweatshirt or, worse, carry a basket with a slogan that includes the words ‘dance’ or ‘love’. Be cautious of words in French. These are the style equivalent of having a ‘Live, laugh, prosecco’ poster in your kitchen. Sorry, but you cannot buy youthful insouciance at M&S.”

articles.title: ‘Such adept cover stars’: why dogs are taking over fashion in the ‘AI face’ era
articles.summary: Cute, egoless canines offer a break from a world that feels dominated by ‘nepo babies’ and ‘Maga lady aesthetic’ What do Nicole Kidman, a pair of “nepo babies” and a beagle called Sansa Martínez Berlingeri have in common?
body: The September covers of British Vogue and Vogue US have come under intense scrutiny after their recent release, while their canine counterpoint, Dogue, has been almost unanimously celebrated.

Dogue this year features Bad Bunny’s beagle, Lena Dunham’s Mexican hairless Ingrid and her Chinese crested Cornichon, and Millie Bobby Brown’s miniature poodle. The Bad Bunny cover, shot by Eric Rojas in the nostalgia-tinged style of Lady and the Tramp, features four-year-old Sansa. She stares winsomely at the camera, one paw held tenderly by her owner, her tongue wonky and a bowl of spaghetti in front of her.

This contrasts with the reception for British Vogue’s Kidman cover, shot by Venetia Scott, in which the appearance of the Australian-American actor led to discussions online over what some argued was excessive airbrushing. Others questioned whether it was an AI version of the Practical Magic star.

articles.title: 29 Easy Chicken Breast Recipes for Fall
articles.summary: Like saucy chicken stroganoff, miso chicken soup with squash, and cranberry chicken stir-fry.
body: In fall, chicken breasts are an easy starting point for all kinds of dinners: crispy cutlets, quick weeknight skillet meals, cozy soups, saucy chicken Parm—and on warm early-fall evenings, there’s still time for one last round of grilled chicken.

Learning how to cook chicken breasts so that they stay moist and tender doesn’t take much practice, just a little technique. Start by buying the best chicken breast you can find. Then follow our tips for frying the crispiest chicken cutlets, learn the key to the juiciest grilled chicken, or check out almost every other way to cook chicken breast.

Because they’re leaner than thighs, chicken breasts can easily overcook. Use an instant-read thermometer to check for doneness (chicken breasts are safely cooked when the thickest part reaches 165°F), and let the meat rest before slicing so the juices redistribute. Sauces and marinades can also help keep chicken breasts flavorful and juicy.

articles.title: Bridal Perfume: How to Choose the Right Fragrance for Your Wedding Day
articles.summary: What is the best fragrance for a wedding day? Five experts share their best tips for choosing a bridal perfume that will allow you to relive the cherished moment again and again.
body: One thing I would happily add to our “ magical DIY wedding under the stars ” on my dad’s ranch? An entirely new-to-me fragrance to help, a decade later, step directly through a portal to that party. Bluebonnets and bonfire smoke set the mood then, and camping out during Texas wildflower season can’t (yet!) be bottled. If I’d chosen to add Frédéric Malle and perfumer Dominique Ropion’s award-winning Portrait of A Lady eau de parfum to my stroll down the grassy aisle, could I now be transported from the comfort of a sectional with a single spritz? Maybe, according to some experts.

“Scent can be a powerful trigger of certain memories,” says Matthew Robison, assistant professor in the department of psychology at the University of Notre Dame. “We remember events with all their associated features, not only the sensory experience, but also the emotions we were experiencing at the time,” he explains, adding that memory is naturally associative, building connections between these sensory experiences and the people, places, and events surrounding them.

articles.title: Your Home’s Getting Dumber—and That’s a Good Thing
articles.summary: Here’s why analog is all the rage, according to top interior designers.
body: In an era when technology appears to have a chokehold on society, it’s natural to assume everything is possible through a tap, swipe, or AI prompt. However, when it comes to a well-appointed home, designers say: Not so fast. While some crave the human touch of hand-painted murals or a masterfully planned plate wall, a growing number of people are sidestepping the smart house for a more primitive setup. Goodbye, intelligent devices and Bluetooth-enabled everything. Welcome back, pared-back appliances and mechanical systems.

Call it what you want—“dumb homes,” “analog interiors,” or “lo-fi spaces”—but many are yearning for a simpler time. Before screens and Siri, to be precise. For Bari Jerauld, founder of Blank Slate Studio, the shift is a “response to overstimulation.”

“We spend so much of our lives on screens and in fast-moving digital environments, so the home has become the one place people desperately want to feel the opposite,” the London-based designer explains. “People are asking for warmth, character, and rooms that feel as though they have a history.”

articles.title: Google Will Soon Let You Tell It What Stories You Want to See in Your Discovery Feed
articles.summary: I don't know what the far future of tech looks like, but I know what's in store for the near future: AI. Specifically, AI that responds to natural language prompts. It's already the reality for many platforms, apps, and services: Rather than doing things yourself, you tell the AI what you want…
body: Google announced a handful of changes coming to its self-named app on Friday. Perhaps most notably among the developments is the new ability to "tune" and "tailor" your Discovery feed to your liking—not by giving feedback for specific articles or sources, but by simply telling Google what news you want to see, and what you don't.

If you aren't happy with Gemini's first interpretation of your instruction, you can refine it before refreshing your feed. You can send another prompt (e.g., "can you focus on eco-friendly and sustainable upgrades?") and see how Gemini responds. You can repeat this process until you're happy with the direction Gemini is taking, then hit "Refresh your feed" to see what it came up with. (Of course, you can tap a three-dot menu again to continue changing the experience.) Google says these updates will roll out "in the coming days."
